core: Editing as selecting, ordering, and timing shots and sounds into a sequence
How cuts and shot duration organize screen space, time, continuity, and rhythm
A descriptive-before-interpretive method for analyzing an edit pattern
supporting: Continuity editing, cutting on action, screen direction, match cuts, and parallel editing
Ellipsis and the distinction between editing, cinematography, mise-en-scène, and sound
The relationship between an individual cut, coverage, sequence structure, and viewer orientation

claims.claim: Film editing selects, arranges, and assembles recorded shots so that their order and relation can communicate across scenes and sequences.
An edit can reorganize apparent space and time; ellipsis omits an interval or event that viewers can infer without seeing every moment.
Continuity editing aims to sustain a legible flow of images and sound, including orientation in screen space and time, without making every cut conspicuous.
Cutting on action joins two views during a continuing action, while matching action, eyeline, screen direction, and coverage can help viewers follow a scene.
Parallel editing alternates between two or more lines of action, so viewers compare their timing or relationship rather than receive one uninterrupted line.
Formal viewing attends to editing, transitions, image, sound, and narrative as connected but distinguishable elements of a moving-image work.
A defensible claim about editing begins by describing the actual order, duration, and relation of shots, then makes a qualified interpretation in the context of the sequence.

unsupportedExistingClaims: No usable editing lesson, evidence packet, or source-linked four-option question set existed for this planned topic.
correctionsNeeded: Created an original, source-grounded lesson that identifies editing as an ordering and timing practice rather than a synonym for all film form.
Added a method that distinguishes observable edit patterns from unsupported universal claims about emotion or creator intent.
Added five source-linked questions with verified four-option answer keys and a balanced answer distribution.
rightsIssues: Both consulted references are openly licensed. The lesson is original synthesis and uses no source prose, film dialogue, clips, screenshots, or stills.
